 Communication Media  
Communication media refers to the physical path  through which data is transmitted from the 
transmitter (sender)  to the receiver . 
The physical path that forms the channel through which data is sent and received is called the 
transmission medium . 
• Communication media plays a very important role in a communication network.  
• It acts as a highway  that carries information from sender to receiver.  
• In computer networks, communication media can be classified into:  
o Guided (Wired) Transmission Media  
o Unguided (Wireless) Transmission Media   
 
Definition of Communication Medium  
A physical path  over which information from transmitter/sender to receiver is transmitted is 
called the transmission medium . 
Transmission media are needed for:  
• Interconnecting network devices  
• Faster communication  
• Reliable delivery of data  
• Secure transmission of data

Guided transmission media uses physical cables  that guide or direct data signals  along a

• Guided media is also known as bounded or wired media . 
• In guided media, signals are transmitted through solid conductors . 
• These media provide better security  since signals are confined within cables.

1. Twisted Pair Cable  
2. Coaxial Cable

 2.4 Multiplexing  
 
Meaning of Multiplexing  
Multiplexing is a communication technique in which multiple independent signals are 
combined together and transmitted over a single communication channel . 
• It allows many users or devices to share the same transmission medium . 
• At the destination, the combined signal is separated into its original individual signals.  
• Multiplexing improves the efficiency and utilization of bandwidth . 
 
Need for Multiplexing  
Multiplexing is required because:  
1. Transmission media are expensive and limited  
2. Bandwidth must be utilized efficiently  
3. Multiple users need to communicate simultaneously  
4. It reduces the overall cost of communica

3. Multiple users need to communicate simultaneously  
4. It reduces the overall cost of communication systems  
5. It increases the data -handling capacity of the network

composite signal  at the sender side.

 2.5 Switching  
Meaning of Switching  
Switching is a technique used in communication networks to transfer data from a source to a 
destination through intermediate nodes . 
• It helps in establishing a communication path  between sender and receiver.  
• Switching is required when a direct connection between devices is not possible.  
• Switching systems decide the best path  for data transmission.  
 
Need for Switching  
Switching is required because:  
1. Direct connection between all devices is impra

d for Switching  
Switching is required because:  
1. Direct connection between all devices is impractical  
2. Efficient utilization of network resources is needed  
3. Multiple users need to communicate simultaneously  
4. Data must be routed dynamically across networks  
5. It reduces cost and complexity of communication systems  
 
Types of Switching Techniques  
There are mainly two types of switching techniques : 
1. Circuit Switching  
2. Packet Switching  
 
1. Circuit Switching  
Definition  
Circuit switching is a switching technique in which a dedicated communication path is 
established between sender and receiver before data transmission begins .

Phases of Circuit Switching  
Circuit switching operates in three phases : 
1. Connection Establishment  
• A dedicated path is created between sender and receiver.  
• Resources are reserved for the entire session.  
2. Data Transfer  
• Data is transmitted continuously over the established path.  
• No delay occurs once transmission starts.  
3. Connection Termination  
• After data transmission, the connection is disconnected.  
• Resources are freed for other users.

Definition  
Packet switching is a technique in which data is divided into small units called packets , and 
each packet is transmitted independently through the network.

e network.

Working of Packet Switching  
1. Message is broken into packets  
2. Each packet contains:  
o Source address  
o Destination address  
o Sequence number  
3. Packets are transmitted independently
